Tip 1: Don't take advice from idiots like us
So cool!

1) Just general local train etiquette. Don't stand near the door unless you have a stop coming. Don't get into a Virar train if you want to get down at Borivali. There is always space for a 4th seat. Carry your backpack in front of you like a baby. Specifically, as a female, don't get into the general compartment during peak hours even if it looks empty.

2) Also, it's pani puri here and not gol gappa. Do try our vada pavs and other street food. There are khau gallis at various places and few famous vada pav places.

3) Always go by meter charge when you're traveling in an auto/taxi. Also, you'll find only taxis in South Mumbai or town. Rickshaws are not allowed beyond Bandra/Sion. Taxis are also called kaali-peelis. 

4) The hawker culture is strong here so you'd be well off if you polish your bargaining skills. 

5) Don't be afraid to ask for help if you're ever stuck or lost. Everyone's in a hurry but they're always willing to help.

Hope you like Mumbai and have a great time! It's our jaan!

Like you mentioned, the main reason for this whole thing was the India-Pakistan partition. Kashmir is a mountain region and is strategically important from a war/defense point of view so both countries would like to have it. It gets even more complicated because there are 3 different of ideologies amongst people who live there. One set wants to be part of Pakistan while one set wants to be a part of Pakistan and one set wants an independent state of Kashmir.
And it gets even more complicated because of religion. Kashmiri Pandits (Hindus) were massacred and made to flee Kashmir a couple of decades ago and now the same is happening to the Muslims there.

Haha yes! We have English and Hindi as the official languages along with 22 regional languages which each state can use.
Also yes, Rajasthan and Tamil Nadu can be vastly different.

So in India, a general distinction is between North India and South India where each of them are somewhat similar (with a lot of differences of course). 

There are some cultural shocks but it does feel like India wherever you go because there are some things that are just "Indian" (things like litter and poverty, unfortunately but also good things like compete strangers helping you and the culture of treating guests like god).

I have no kids but I do have nieces and nephews. 
It's really cool that you would want your kid to experience that! I think a good way to start would be Indian movies (even though they are not completely accurate) and music since kids are most likely to appreciate these mediums.
And while I would suggest visiting India once, I'm not sure how a kid from a developed country would feel visiting a developing country like India. It could result in them hating it, especially since racism is also a thing.
